title: Dark Keeper
html:
[Th-then give it your best shot, everyone! Ehehehe!]

With those parting words, the dokkaebi disappeared.

A food penalty and a survival penalty.

I already knew about the former. But although the latter was very much in keeping with Ways of Survival, it hadn't happened in the original.

I could only guess that perhaps my contract with Bihyung had affected how things unfolded.

After checking that the pieces of biscuit in her pocket had disappeared, Jung Heewon asked in a dazed voice.

“Dokja-ssi, I'm just asking on the off chance, but did you know things would turn out this way―”

“I expected it. I thought about what those dokkaebi bastards would do first to torment humans.”

“······Shouldn't you set up shop as a fortune-teller?”

I called Lee Hyunsung and the others over. The situation was in place. Now it was time to move.

“Give us back our food!”

“How, how could this happen?”

The people in the marginalized group were crying out. Cheon Inho and the mainstream group also seemed stunned by the sudden food shortage. When our eyes met, Cheon Inho bit his lip.

「Could he······ have known? No, that's impossible.」

If I could read his mind, that was surely what he would be thinking.

[You have accurately read the inner thoughts of the character ‘Cheon Inho.’]

[Your understanding of the character ‘Cheon Inho’ has increased.]

···Something like this increased my understanding?

As a test, I looked at other people's expressions and tried to guess their thoughts. But messages like the ones before didn't appear so readily.

Meanwhile, Cheon Inho was swiftly bringing the confusion under control and gathering people together.

“Everyone, please gather around. I have an urgent announcement.”

The announcement was simple. Since the situation had worsened, they would draft more people from the marginalized group into the ‘scouting party.’ He must have been feeling the pressure. There was no food left underground now.

“From now on, we will not distribute food to anyone who does not join the ‘scouting party.’”

Despite the hard-line declaration, the citizens didn't particularly protest. No, they couldn't. An inevitable result under these circumstances, I supposed.

The people who had been watching hesitantly began volunteering for the scouting party, one by one.

That was why hope remained on Cheon Inho's face despite the disappearance of the food. The more desperate the situation became, the more control would pass to the mainstream group.

Watching this uneasily, Lee Hyunsung spoke.

“Dokja-ssi, what should we do now?”

“Go find food, of course.”

At those words, tension settled over my companions' faces. Finding food. That could mean only one thing.

“Should we join the scouting party too, then? There's still food left aboveground.”

“No, we're not going aboveground. If we go that way, we'll definitely die.”

I looked at the emergency gas masks strewn across the floor. There was no way those tattered masks could keep out the deadly poison fog.

“But to find food, we need to go aboveground······.”

“Lee Hyunsung-ssi. The world has changed. What we eat needs to change too.”

I looked toward the tunnel leading to Yaksu Station.

“Wait a moment. Dokja-ssi······ don't tell me?”

“That's right.”

In this world, humans were no longer apex predators.

But not being a predator didn't necessarily mean you had to become prey.

“We're going to hunt monsters.”

*

A little later, several people from the marginalized group, myself included, stood in front of the tunnel leading toward Yaksu Station.

“I see. You're going down the tracks?”

Since I had refused to join the scouting party, I'd naturally expected Cheon Inho to object. Instead, he seemed relieved that I would be roaming outside the group. Perhaps he thought I would pose a threat to his power.

“Well, in the long run, we do need a team dedicated to clearing scenarios. Have a safe trip.”

What a joke.

He talked as though he were the leader. But he wouldn't be so relaxed for much longer.

[Your understanding of the character ‘Cheon Inho’ has increased.]

[Your understanding of the character ‘Cheon Inho’ has reached a certain level.]

I see······. Now I understood.

There were two main cases in which my ‘understanding’ of a character increased.

One, when I gained a character's goodwill or trust.

Two, when I accurately guessed a character's inner thoughts.

This was probably the latter.

[The character ‘Cheon Inho’ is suspicious of your motives.]

And depending on how much understanding I accumulated, it seemed I could also learn a character's vague thoughts and feelings.

“Oh, since you're going, could you take one of our group members along? We'd like to obtain some information about clearing the scenario too.”

As expected, Cheon Inho wouldn't let us go so easily.

I looked at the man who emerged hesitantly from the back. Of all people, he was the one coming with us. What an unlucky bastard.

“D-do I really have to go along?”

“Come on, why are you acting like this now, Han-hyung? Haven't you been begging since last night to make up with Dokja-ssi?”

“Th-that's······.”

The member of Cheon Inho's group joining us was none other than Department Head Han Myungoh.

“W-well, Dokja-ssi. If you don't mind, I'd like to come along too······.”

“Sure. Let's go together.”

Han Myungoh looked astonished at my ready agreement. He must have assumed I'd refuse.

Lee Hyunsung looked concerned beside me, but I had thought this through.

Anyway, that brought the total to five: me, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Gilyoung, Yoo Sangah, and Han Myungoh. In other words, the party of survivors from carriage ‘3807’ had re-formed.

“I can come too, right?”

“···You haven't recovered yet. Will you be all right?”

“This much won't faze me.”

And one more. To be precise, a party of six including Jung Heewon. A small number or a large one, depending on how you looked at it.

Grrrr······.

Of course, numbers wouldn't matter much in the face of the crisis soon to come.

[A new sub-scenario has arrived.]

+

<Sub-scenario ― Food Acquisition>

Category : Main

Difficulty : E

Clear Conditions : Personally hunt a monster that can be used as food, then cook it.

Time Limit : None

Reward : 500 coins

Failure : ???

+

The sub-scenario arrived the moment we stepped into the tunnel.

Food Acquisition. A sub-scenario we had to go through before entering the second main scenario.

[A few constellations look forward to your performance.]

Before we had taken even ten steps, the tunnel was completely dark. Even with a flashlight shining into it, we couldn't make out any of our surroundings.

Proof that a light-blocking veil stood before us. The real thing would be beyond that veil.

“Dokja-ssi, wait a moment. It's really dangerous from here on.”

Jung Heewon, walking beside me, was the first to stop.

“You're not just going to walk in like this, are you? It looks like suicide any way I look at it. And Gilyoung's here too.”

“Actually, that's been bothering me for a while too. It's not too late, so why don't we take Gilyoung back? And the women too, if possible······.”

“Lee Hyunsung-ssi, I might not be as good as you, but I can fight pretty well, you know? I used to practice kendo too.”

“But······.”

Since this unnecessary argument seemed about to heat up, I cut in at a suitable moment.

“Lee Hyunsung-ssi. Didn't I tell you earlier? The world has changed. The idea that women are physically weak is a prejudice. Anyone can become stronger now by raising their overall stats. But Jung Heewon-ssi, there's a flaw in what you said too, Heewon-ssi.”

“······What is it?”

“Being a woman doesn't necessarily make someone weak. Neither does being a child. Gilyoung, show them.”

Lee Gilyoung stepped forward. He looked around briefly, then sat down on the tunnel floor and held out his hand. Jung Heewon's eyes widened.

“Good heavens, what's that?”

“F-fuck! It's a cockroach!”

Han Myungoh shouted in horror.

A cockroach making a skittering sound was connected to Lee Gilyoung's fingertip by a faint, unbroken line. It listened to him as though it were an obedient puppy, then disappeared into the darkness.

“My attribute is ‘Insect Collector.’”

Insect Collector. Lee Gilyoung possessed a rare ability that let him communicate in simple terms with insects through the [Diverse Communication] skill.

“It says there's nothing up ahead. We should be safe for the next hundred steps.”

My companions looked dumbfounded at Lee Gilyoung's overwhelming scouting ability. With a bold expression, he continued speaking to them.

“Thank you for worrying about me, but I didn't come along to have you hyungs and noonas carry me.”

“Oh, right.”

Jung Heewon nodded with an awkward expression. Lee Gilyoung promptly came back to my side, and I patted his head.

Lee Gilyoung's ability was an attribute I'd never seen even in the original Ways of Survival. Saving him early on had certainly been no mistake. We passed through the transparent barrier and entered the darkness proper.

[Entering a danger zone.]

“Y-Yoo Sangah-ssi. It's dangerous, so hold my hand while we walk.”

“······You seem more frightened than I am, Department Head-nim.”

“N-no, I'm not!”

The air inside the veil was sticky with humidity.

“Dim the light.”

At my words, Yoo Sangah immediately covered the flashlight. It was a model with no brightness adjustment, so she had no choice but to control the light with her hand.

“Urgh. Don't shine it down there.”

Jung Heewon retched after seeing the floor. Bodies that had been torn into and eaten. The corpses of people who had tried to head toward Yaksu without knowing any better lay everywhere, so thickly that we could trip over them.

Yoo Sangah squeezed her eyes shut, Han Myungoh trembled, and even the courageous Lee Hyunsung let out a low groan.

Surprisingly, Lee Gilyoung was unperturbed. There wasn't a trace of fear on the child's face. It left me a little uneasy.

Could this kid think it was all a game?

“Some of them aren't human.”

As Lee Gilyoung said, there were more than human corpses on the floor. About the size of full-grown wolves. The carcasses of mole-like creatures with well-developed forelegs lay scattered here and there.

Grade 9 subterranean species, ground rats.

The name brought to mind an insect from Earth, but a name was just a name. These things were like underground piranhas. Ground rats were relentless hunters that tunneled and moved in packs, stalking their prey.

Yet those ground rats lay sprawled out as though they'd been bombed. Jung Heewon spoke with a sigh.

“······Who on earth did this to them?”

Naturally, there was only one human nearby who could leave ground rats in this state.

Yoo Joonghyuk.

He had forced his way through this route alone and moved on to the next station.

But something puzzled me. The third-round Yoo Joonghyuk was originally supposed to move to the next station this evening or tomorrow.

Why had he been in such a hurry?

Had he suddenly grown impatient?

Because of what?

“Dokja-ssi, couldn't we use these as food?”

“The scenario said we have to hunt them ‘personally,’ so I don't think these will count.”

“······True, it does feel a little unpleasant. What about cooking them? Would roasting them over a fire work?”

Roasting them would work. The problem was that it had to be a special fire.

“More to the point, Heewon-ssi, you said you were good at kendo, right?”

“Uh, actually, saying I'm good at it would be a bit······. But what are you doing now?”

After stabbing a ground rat's corpse with my spike, I began cutting it open with a knife. I hadn't realized it when reading the novel, but it wasn't as easy as I'd imagined.

Still, I somehow peeled off its tough hide and succeeded in cutting out the spine inside. Since it was my first time, I'd left plenty of nicks, but it should be usable enough as it was.

“What are you going to use that for?”

“You need a weapon to practice kendo.”

It wasn't as good as a stone hog's spike, but a ground rat's spine consisted of a single solid bone, making it a fairly good weapon early in the scenarios.

After cutting away the remaining cartilage connecting it to the legs and shaping it, the bone really did look quite like a sword. I placed it in Jung Heewon's hand.

“Thank you. I suddenly feel like I'm back in the Paleolithic era.”

“You'll need to sharpen it a little more for it to be useful. If there's a stone or something nearby, try giving it a proper edge.”

“Hehe, understood, Chief-nim.”

Sounding a little excited, Jung Heewon immediately began sharpening the blade. Watching her, Lee Hyunsung looked toward me, apparently envious.

“Would you like me to make you one?”

“Oh, you'll make one for me too?”

“Everyone else, come closer too. It's a good idea to learn how. Let's all make them together.”

In truth, this was my first time doing anything like this too. If Ways of Survival hadn't described monster butchering in detail, I wouldn't even have dared attempt it.

Why wasn't Ways of Survival popular? Simple. The author was a worldbuilding nerd.

“······Dokja-ssi, your hands move like a beginner's, but you're strangely good at this.”

We sat down and made weapons together. This time, though, we made spears rather than swords. Since the others didn't have the [Kendo] skill, I judged that spears with their longer reach would be safer to handle.

I gave the one made from the largest ground rat's spine to Lee Hyunsung, and those made from average-sized spines to Yoo Sangah and Han Myungoh. Lastly, I made Lee Gilyoung a club with a baby ground rat's skull mounted on it.

[You have successfully obtained weapons through your own efforts.]

[A very small number of constellations take an interest in humanity's primitive nature.]

[The constellations have donated 100 coins.]

This time, everyone received the messages together.

“They give us coins even for something like this.”

“It's not as though we're simply meant to die. You all have some coins of your own, right?”

“Yes, I do.”

“If possible, keep only enough coins for the survival fee and invest all the rest in Strength, Constitution, and Agility. You won't be able to survive otherwise.”

“Ah, I'll keep that in mind.”

Once our preparations were complete, we began advancing again. We were almost at the end of the hundred steps Lee Gilyoung had mentioned.

[Sub-scenario― Food Acquisition begins!]

Ground rats crawled out of the floor one after another. I quickly counted them. One, two, three······. Exactly thirteen. More than I'd expected.

Grrrr······.

The pack of ground rats crept forward, marking out a line as they began threatening us. The moment we crossed that line, the fight would begin.

“We don't have any particular plan. This is our first time here, and it may sound cruel, but honestly, I don't expect you to survive.”

“Th-that's······.”

“Even so, all of you, survive. Please.”

Han Myungoh was the only one among my companions who looked flustered. The others were tense, but their expressions were quite determined. The look in Jung Heewon's eyes was especially something to see.

“All right, let's give it a shot. Let's all live to see each other again!”

Just as Yoo Joonghyuk had put me to the test, I had expectations of these people too. No matter how excellent an adviser you had beside you, you couldn't survive in this world without firm resolve.

In the end, you were the one who saved yourself.

Everyone had to take this opportunity to understand that clearly.

“Then let's go.”

And I, too, would be able to tell which of them I should take with me.

When I took one more step, the ground rats moved.

The fight began.

My companions fought well.

In fact, well enough to surprise me a little.

In particular, Lee Hyunsung's decision to join me at the front without being told, and Jung Heewon's decision to coordinate with him, proved very effective.

The battle naturally took shape with the three of us at the front and the remaining three covering the rear.

Thwack!

Less than 1 minute into the battle, several ground rats lay on the floor with their throats pierced.

After taking down another charging ground rat, Lee Hyunsung wiped the sweat from his forehead and spoke.

“······I think we can do this.”

Once they raised their overall stats, humans weren't so weak.

Even so, Lee Hyunsung's mental fortitude was something quite special in this world. An ordinary human couldn't remain so calm when faced with monsters.

He wouldn't earn the name ‘Steel Sword Emperor’ later for nothing.

But Jung Heewon was even more surprising.

“Their attack patterns are simpler than I expected.”

Yelp!

Apparently her [Kendo] skill wasn't just for show. Every time the tip of her sword struck, a ground rat lost a leg, a tail, or some other part.

“Haaah!”

Jung Heewon had invested all the coins she'd recently accumulated in Strength. Her endurance was poor, but each individual blow was more powerful than I'd expected.

Whoosh!

No sooner had I thought that than her sword cut through empty air.

“Damn it, one got past me! Take care of it!”

Her voice shook, perhaps because she was out of breath. Her only weakness was probably her lack of endurance due to her low Constitution level.

Grrrr!

The ground rat that barged in among my companions despite its injuries was fairly clever. Having succeeded in breaking up our formation, it followed its hunter's instincts and lunged at the opponent who looked weakest.

“Leave it to me.”

But the ground rat didn't know it had chosen the wrong opponent.

Thwack!

The club swung by Lee Gilyoung's two small hands jolted the ground rat's head. Being a child, he lacked striking power, but that was enough. The others could help finish it off.

Shunk!

The sharpened tip of Yoo Sangah's spear pierced the ground rat's torso. It writhed several times. Yoo Sangah looked distressed, but she didn't loosen her grip on the spear.

Whiiine······.

Its strength exhausted, the ground rat went limp.

Honestly, I'd thought Yoo Sangah would have trouble adapting, so this really was unexpected. Normally, panicking like Han Myungoh standing over there would be the natural response.

“U-ughhh······.”

Even as the others fought hard, Han Myungoh was busy hiding at the back. He hadn't even managed to hide properly, and was bleeding from a bite around his shin.

Yelp······ squeak!

The last ground rat was pierced by my spike, and our surroundings soon fell quiet. Shaking the blood off the spike, I looked over my companions. Aside from Han Myungoh, everyone had minor scrapes but no serious wounds.

It was an excellent first victory.

With the tension gone, Yoo Sangah and Lee Gilyoung sank to the ground. Lee Hyunsung planted his spear in the floor and wiped the sweat from his forehead. Counting the ground rats strewn around us, Jung Heewon let out a sigh.

“······Dokja-ssi, how many did you kill all by yourself?”

“Four.”

“Tch, I only got two.”

“I got three as well.”

Watching Lee Hyunsung proudly display the tip of his spear somehow hurt my pride.

Even though I hadn't gone all out, a difference of only one?

I activated my skill and took a furtive look at Lee Hyunsung's Attributes Window.

+

<Character Information>

Name : Lee Hyunsung

Age : 28

Constellation Sponsor (背後星) : Master of Steel

Exclusive Attribute : Soldier who Turned a Blind Eye to Injustice (General)

Exclusive Skills : [Bayonet Skills Lv.2], [Camouflage Lv.1], [Patience Lv.1], [Sense of Justice Lv.1], [Weapons Training Lv.2]

Stigma : [Great Mountain Push Lv.1]

Overall Stats : [Constitution Lv.12], [Strength Lv.9], [Agility Lv.9], [Magic Power Lv.6]

Overall Evaluation : An opportunity for attribute evolution is gradually approaching. This individual has considerable trust in you. This individual's constellation sponsor is wary of you.

●The ‘Starter Pack’ is currently in effect.

+

Huh, a ‘Starter Pack.’

No wonder he was strong.

The Master of Steel seemed quite taken with Lee Hyunsung.

The Starter Pack was a coin package that could be used when an incarnation's average overall stat level was below 10.

A good item pack that immediately raised each overall stat by 1 level upon use, while also allowing the user to learn [Weapons Training], a proficiency skill useful in the early stages.

Considering that most incarnations were exploited as free-to-play users without so much as a Starter Pack, Lee Hyunsung could be considered extraordinarily lucky.

“Dokja-ssi, you don't look well······.”

“Oh, no. I was just thinking for a moment.”

I was a little envious······ but, well, it wasn't that I couldn't afford it. I was choosing not to buy it. With my average overall stat level already well above 10, buying it now would only be a loss for me.

Damn it, if only I'd opened the Dokkaebi Bag a little earlier.

“Let's gather up the ground rats we killed first. We need to prepare today's food.”

“Hmm······. But how do we cook these? We can't eat them like this.”

“We can't eat them now, but there should be a way.”

Had I answered too calmly?

For a moment, silence fell among my companions. Lee Hyunsung was the first to speak.

“Um, actually, there's something I'd like to ask you.”

“Yes?”

“Dokja-ssi, do you perhaps······ know something about this situation?”

I realized I'd slipped up.

“Well······.”

Suddenly, I thought of the regressors in the novels I'd read, then Yoo Joonghyuk's face came to mind.

So this was it. How regressors felt.

What did regressors usually say at times like this?

A few stock responses came to mind. Some brazenly replied, “It's just a hunch.” Others lied, as I had to Yoo Joonghyuk.

[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ looks forward to your choice.]

[A few constellations look forward to your answer.]

But if I may be so bold as to speak from a reader's perspective, the best answer was.

“A-aaaargh!”

To keep creating situations in which you didn't have to answer.

[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ nods at your choice.]

“There was still one left!”

Jung Heewon shouted, and Lee Hyunsung ran. But the ground rat that had been hiding moved faster than anyone. It was far larger than the others.

Chomp―

“H-help meee······!”

The ground rat seized Han Myungoh's leg and dragged him toward the burrow it had emerged from. Yoo Sangah, who was closest, swung her spear, but the terrified Han Myungoh threw his arms around her, making the situation even worse.

“Grab this!”

Lee Hyunsung belatedly extended the shaft of his spear, but it merely gouged the innocent floor.

The ground rat and the two people had already disappeared beneath the floor.

[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is outraged by the inevitable frustration.]

Jung Heewon vented her frustration.

“Ah··· I thought that man was going to give me cancer. Seriously.”

“······I'm sorry. I was too late.”

Lee Hyunsung spoke in a somber voice. I patted his shoulder to show him it was all right.

“No one could have done anything.”

“Should we go after them?”

I examined the burrow the creature had vanished into. It wasn't an ordinary burrow. The air had a palpable texture. It felt as though darkness had been finely ground into it.

Pretending to think, I stepped back and discreetly turned on my smartphone.

The remaining battery was a little over 5%. That was the charge I'd received from people in the marginalized group at dawn in exchange for one portion of food.

[Your reading speed increases due to your attribute's effect!]

Before long, I found the passage I wanted.

「······The [Dark Fold], where ground rats live, is a kind of subspace (亞空間) emitted by the [Dark Root], a tree of the Demon Realm. Ground rats breathe black ether instead of oxygen and cannot survive on their own anywhere away from the [Dark Fold]······」

I knew the general facts already, but there was still value in reviewing them.

I see.

This was the entrance to the [Dark Fold].

I finished reading the relevant passages and put my smartphone in my pocket.

“Dokja-ssi?”

Lee Hyunsung was watching me anxiously. I nodded.

“We're going in.”

“Ah, then······.”

“But it's too risky for a large number of us to go in. Lee Hyunsung-ssi and Jung Heewon-ssi, please stay here and keep watch in all directions. I'll signal you if anything happens.”

Startled, Jung Heewon asked.

“Don't tell me······ you're going in with just Gilyoung?”

“Gilyoung's ability will help us track it.”

Just as she was about to protest vehemently, I raised a hand and called to Lee Hyunsung.

“And Lee Hyunsung-ssi. Jung Heewon-ssi isn't in good condition, so please take good care of her.”

At those words, Lee Hyunsung seemed to realize something too.

“Understood.”

“Wait a moment. I'm telling you, I'm fine!”

“Jung Heewon-ssi, confidence is good, but don't be reckless.”

“······.”

Jung Heewon couldn't catch her breath. She hadn't yet fully recovered from the deadly poison fog's effects.

Leaving the two behind, I took Lee Gilyoung into the burrow. Although it had clearly been dug downward at a nearly vertical angle, the moment we entered, we could stand and walk as though gravity had taken hold.

It was because of the magic power emitted by the [Dark Fold].

“This way.”

The darkness was so thick that I couldn't see an inch ahead, so I advanced relying solely on Lee Gilyoung's fingertips. Black ether absorbed light, making the flashlight useless too. Without Lee Gilyoung's [Diverse Communication] ability, I might have had to spend coins again.

“Um, hyung.”

Lee Gilyoung called to me.

“You did that on purpose earlier, didn't you?”

“······Did what?”

“When that monster took noona and the man, you let it happen on purpose.”

I hesitated for a moment. Lee Gilyoung's fingertips touching me in the darkness felt unfamiliar. Before I could ask how he'd known, he continued explaining.

“I was watching your face then.”

He'd been watching me even in that brief moment? What a frightening kid. There was no point trying to hide things from someone this perceptive.

“Yes, that's right.”

No sooner had I answered than a barrage of messages flooded my head. Well, this would make a useful spectacle for those constellation bastards too.

[The constellations of the Absolute Good alignment frown at your cruelty.]

[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ urges you on with gleaming eyes.]

“Why did you do it?”

“Because of the ground rats' habits.”

I decided to answer honestly.

“Ground rats have a habit of stockpiling what they capture in one place. They collect quite a few things that look valuable, as well as food. Items, for instance. But the routes to their stockpiles are so complicated that you can't find them unless you follow a path the rats have dug themselves.”

Lee Gilyoung was silent for a moment. I continued.

“I expected it to take Han Myungoh. I didn't expect Yoo Sangah-ssi to get dragged along too.”

“Then your goal isn't to save noona and the man. It's the items, right?”

“Yes. Are you disappointed?”

“No.”

I felt Lee Gilyoung's small hand grip my finger tightly.

“You're not very good at lying, hyung.”

“······.”

“If you really were that kind of person, you wouldn't have saved me on the subway either. I trust you, hyung.”

Lee Gilyoung didn't act like a child, but he was still only a child.

Lee Gilyoung didn't know.

That acting grown-up and becoming an adult were entirely different things.

[Some constellations are moved to tears.]

[You have received a donation of 200 coins.]

And that this world was full of despicable adults who could exploit that ‘grown-up behavior’ as much as they pleased.

The burrow was longer than I'd expected, and we had to descend for quite some time.

“Um, hyung.”

“Yeah.”

“Are you a god, by any chance?”

“······What?”

“Or are you the ‘protagonist’?”

Children sometimes asked incisive questions. Was it because they lived in a world where metaphor and reality weren't clearly distinguished? Lee Gilyoung probably didn't know exactly what his question meant.

“I'm neither a god nor the protagonist. If anything, I always envied the protagonist.”

“But you do know something about this world, right?”

After a moment's thought, I answered.

“That's true.”

“Then I'll ask you just one thing.”

“If it's something I can answer.”

“Once we clear all these scenarios······ can we have a wish come true?”

“A wish?”

I was a little taken aback.

“There's usually a reward like that at the end of stories like this. There's something like that at the end of this story too, right?”

Lee Gilyoung's breathing trembled in the darkness.

Suddenly, I remembered his expression as he looked at his dead mother.

Those who had adapted to this world suffered from it in different ways. Some through madness, some through fanaticism, and others through irrational optimism.

“Yes, there is.”

I was grateful we were in such deep darkness.

Because there was no way Lee Gilyoung could see my expression now.

“We're almost there, hyung.”

The black ether around us was rapidly thinning. Proof that the [Dark Root] was nearby. Tensing, I drew my spike.

[A very small number of constellations hold their breath.]

From somewhere came the sound of ground rats digging into the floor. As the sounds drew closer, the space around us seemed to widen rapidly. Through the darkness, I could see the light of a fire that looked as though someone had lit it.

And beyond that firelight, a single dingy black chest.

The moment I felt certain we'd come to the right place, messages rang in my ears.

[The sub-scenario has been updated.]

[You have entered the ‘Ground Rats' Treasure Storehouse.’]

“Hyung! That's······.”

Just before Lee Gilyoung could speak after spotting the treasure chest, I covered his small mouth.

“Shh, wait.”

The world of Ways of Survival was merciless. The constellations enjoyed the characters' hardships, and every obstacle in the scenarios was perfectly suited to fucking humans over.

Things like that, practically saying “Come and gobble me up,” were usually traps. You couldn't trust even the system messages.

“Just because it's a treasure storehouse doesn't mean there's only treasure inside.”

[The constellation, ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ is disappointed.]

Abyssal Black Flame Dragon······.

It seemed that bastard had been hoping I'd drop dead for a while now.

Anyway, I waited.

Before long, shadows began appearing one by one, prowling around the treasure storehouse.

Grrrr······ squeak!

They were ground rats. They'd brought loads of something through the tunnels and were exchanging information through incomprehensible cries.

Fwoosh.
